items: Restaurant business intelligence pulls sales, labor, inventory, guest feedback and financial data into one view, so you see what's happening at each location, why, and what to do about it.
Connected data keeps you from fixing the wrong problem: a revenue drop that looks like a staffing issue can turn out to be new menu items slowing the kitchen.
Choose tools by the areas you need to track, whether guest experience, sales and revenue, labor, inventory or operations, since most platforms cover only some of them.
Look for location benchmarking, forecasting and automated reports, so you spot underperforming stores early and act before small issues cost you revenue.
